nodes.name: Intake Form
nodes.notes: STAGE: input/intake. A human starts one analysis run by submitting this form. No file content is embedded in the workflow -- paths are supplied at submission time (see setup docs: PFA_PROJECT_ROOT).

parameters.formDescription: Paths are resolved on the n8n host, relative to PFA_PROJECT_ROOT (see setup docs). This step only runs analysis -- it never creates a GitHub issue.

nodes.name: Build Analysis Command
nodes.notes: Builds the product-feedback-agent CLI invocation (Stage 13 orchestrator). No analysis logic lives here -- it only shell-quotes the form inputs.

nodes.name: Run Analysis (Python CLI)
nodes.notes: STAGE: analysis invocation. Runs the reusable orchestrator CLI (analyst -> deterministic validator -> critic -> optional single revision). No core product logic is duplicated in n8n. The CLI writes ONLY the structured JSON result to stdout; the human-review notice goes to stderr.

nodes.name: Parse Orchestration Result
nodes.notes: Fails the run loudly on a non-zero exit code rather than presenting a partial/garbled result for approval.

nodes.name: Render Review Summary
nodes.notes: STAGE: structured opportunity display. Renders exactly the 3 opportunities, their deterministic scores, evidence counts, and unresolved validation issues -- nothing here re-scores or re-decides anything.

nodes.name: Human Review & Approval
nodes.notes: STAGE: explicit human approval boundary. This is the ONLY step that can authorize a GitHub write. Approval is never inferred -- the human must type 'approve' AND name one opportunity_id AND the target repo. Any other input (including leaving this blank/timing out) is treated as reject by the Approval Gate below.

values.fieldLabel: opportunity_id to act on (leave blank to reject)

nodes.name: Approval Gate
nodes.notes: STAGE: approve/reject branch. Only the exact string 'approve' from the human review form continues to the GitHub-action branch. Everything else (including 'reject', blank, or malformed input) goes to the no-action branch. Deterministic validation is never bypassed here -- it already ran, unconditionally, before this gate.

conditions.leftValue: ={{ $json['opportunity_id to act on (leave blank to reject)'] }}

nodes.name: Build GitHub Action Command
nodes.notes: Approved path only. Writes the ORIGINAL orchestration result (not a re-derived or n8n-edited version) to a run-scoped temp file, then calls the Stage 14 github_action CLI with --approved --no-dry-run and an allow-list containing ONLY the human-supplied repo. No core GitHub logic is duplicated here -- this only shells out to the existing Python CLI.

nodes.name: Create GitHub Issue (Approved)
nodes.notes: STAGE: GitHub action, approved path only. This node is unreachable unless Approval Gate matched 'approve' with a named opportunity_id and repo. The underlying CLI independently re-checks approved/dry-run/allow-list/duplicate before ever calling GitHub -- this node cannot bypass those guards.

nodes.name: Approved Summary
nodes.notes: status will be 'created', 'refused_duplicate', 'refused_unsupported_repo', or 'refused_not_approved' -- inspect this before assuming an issue was actually filed.

nodes.name: No Action (Rejected)
nodes.notes: STAGE: rejected/no-action path. Reached whenever the human did not type 'approve' with both an opportunity_id and a repo. Intentionally connects to nothing further -- no GitHub node exists on this branch, so no mutation is structurally possible from here.
